claims.text: Tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys strengthened through stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations can exhibit ultrahigh strength and tensile ductility.
Adding a lubricious phase to a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy can produce self-lubricating behavior over a wide temperature range.
The tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy is prepared through conventional metallurgical routes.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations enhance the strength and ductility of tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
A tungsten-disulfide-like lubricious phase can be formed in situ or dispersed within the tungsten-based RHEA during processing.
The proposed material is suitable for operation from room temperature to well above 800 °C.
Coherent SCCP interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
Combining coherent nanoprecipitates with a controlled lubricious-phase dispersion reduces friction at sliding interfaces.
The tungsten-based refractory alloy matrix maintains high mechanical integrity at elevated temperature.
The added lubricious phase forms a self-adaptive, low-friction surface during sliding.
The lubricious phase provides a lubricating interface layer that balances reduced friction with the matrix's load-bearing capacity.
The modified alloy will retain ultrahigh strength and ductility after incorporation of the lubricious phase.
The modified alloy will have significantly lower friction and wear at both low and high temperatures than an otherwise similar alloy without the lubricious phase.
Tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys without an added lubricious phase can exhibit excellent high-temperature strength.
Tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys without an added lubricious phase do not optimize lubrication performance.
An excessive or poorly controlled lubricious-phase addition can undermine the alloy's load-bearing properties.
